lead.tldr: US Senate advances Clarity Act, bipartisan 15‑9 vote, signaling regulatory momentum for crypto market structure • SBI and Rakuten plan crypto investment trusts and ETFs pending FSA approval, could unlock Japanese institutional demand • VerifiedX's Bitcoin reliever chain targets programmable, privacy‑preserving DeFi, aiming to expand BTC DeFi beyond $5 B

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, the US Senate moves the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act closer to law, Japan’s major brokers prepare crypto ETFs, and VerifiedX is building a Bitcoin sidechain for native, private DeFi. Stay tuned for the impact on capital flows and innovation.

top_signals.title: The Clarity Act took a step forward: State of Crypto
top_signals.summary: The US Senate Banking Committee voted 15‑9 to advance the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act to the Senate floor. The vote included all Republicans and two Democrats, indicating growing bipartisan support for a clearer regulatory framework for digital assets. The bill, which aims to establish market‑structure rules for crypto, still requires additional approvals and potential compromises before it can become law, a development that institutional investors are watching closely.

top_signals.title: Japan's SBI Securities, Rakuten Securities to offer crypto investment trusts, ETFs
top_signals.summary: SBI Securities and Rakuten Securities have announced that they will introduce cryptocurrency investment trusts and exchange‑traded funds in Japan. The products will be launched after the Financial Services Agency completes its pending regulatory framework for digital assets. A Nikkei survey indicates that eleven additional major securities firms are monitoring the same regulatory progress and are prepared to roll out comparable offerings. The move reflects a broader shift toward institutional‑grade crypto investment vehicles in the Japanese market.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin DeFi's new front: VerifiedX bets BTC's next chapter is programmable and private
top_signals.summary: VerifiedX is building a Bitcoin sidechain called a reliever chain that seeks to deliver native, programmable and privacy‑preserving DeFi on Bitcoin without relying on wrapped assets. The design uses self‑custodial threshold signatures and Taproot‑based addresses to retain Bitcoin’s security model. Bitcoin DeFi currently holds just over $5 billion, indicating a sizable market. By adding programmable and private capabilities, the project aims to expand Bitcoin’s utility and attract institutional capital to the ecosystem.

linkedin_post: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, Exciting signals are emerging across the globe that could shape the next wave of crypto investment. In Washington, the US Senate Banking Committee voted 15‑9 to move the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act to the Senate floor. The vote brought together every Republican and two Democrats, showing a growing bipartisan appetite for a clearer regulatory framework. While the bill still needs further approvals and likely compromises, institutional investors are already gauging the impact on market‑structure rules. Across the Pacific, Japan’s SBI Securities and Rakuten Securities announced plans to launch cryptocurrency investment trusts and ETFs once the Financial Services Agency finalises its pending framework. A recent Nikkei survey revealed that eleven other major securities firms are watching the same developments and stand ready to introduce comparable products. This momentum points to a broader shift toward institutional‑grade crypto vehicles in a market that has traditionally been retail‑focused. Meanwhile, on the technical frontier, VerifiedX is building a Bitcoin reliever chain that promises native, programmable and privacy‑preserving DeFi without relying on wrapped assets. By leveraging self‑custodial threshold signatures and Taproot‑based addresses, the project aims to keep Bitcoin’s security model intact while expanding its utility. With Bitcoin DeFi already holding just over $5 billion, the potential to attract more institutional capital is compelling. At Blockwall we see these trends converging into a powerful catalyst for European founders building the next generation of compliant, scalable crypto solutions.
